# Cross-owner metadata write via POST /duplicates/resolve

## Summary

Any registered user can write to another user's asset rows. The authorization check on
`POST /duplicates/resolve` asks whether the caller owns *any* asset carrying a given duplicate-group UUID,
and the caller can make that true for herself with one ordinary update to her own asset. Once inside the
group, the merge writes attacker-chosen description, rating, favourite flag, GPS coordinates and tag
associations onto assets she does not own.

Confirmed on the released `v3.1.0` image, `sourceCommit 8aa95c67`. Still present on main at `a9a99cff`.

## The asymmetry

Three functions in `server/src/repositories/duplicate.repository.ts`:

```ts
async delete(userId: string, id: string)       // line 158, .where('ownerId', '=', userId)
async deleteAll(userId: string, ids: string[]) // line 168, .where('ownerId', '=', userId)
async get(duplicateId: string)                 // line 115, no ownerId predicate, no userId parameter
```

`get` is the read that feeds the write path. It filters on `duplicateId`, `deletedAt` and `stackId` and
nothing else, so it returns every user's assets in the group.

Your own commit `d4f29ab6a`, "validate duplicate group ownership before dismissal" from 2026-05-04, added
`requireAccess` to `delete` and `deleteAll`. Both of those already had `ownerId` in their SQL, so the check
was belt over braces. `resolve` landed earlier in `8c6adf715` and shipped in v2.7.0. It got the same
`requireAccess` call but has no SQL backstop, so there the check is the entire control surface.

And that check is satisfiable by the caller. `Permission.DuplicateDelete` routes to
`access.duplicate.checkOwnerAccess`, which is `where duplicateId in (...) and ownerId = :userId`. It asks
whether you own anything in the group, not whether you may write the rows you are about to write.
`duplicateId` is an ordinary field on the bulk asset update DTO, so one `PUT /assets` on your own asset
joins any group you can name.

`resolveGroup` then checks `Permission.AssetDelete` on `idsToTrash`, `Permission.AssetShare` on `idsToKeep`
for the album side effect, and `Permission.TagAsset` on the merged tags. It checks nothing at all on
`idsToKeep` before:

```ts
await this.assetRepository.updateAllExif(idsToKeep, exifUpdate);
await this.assetRepository.updateAll(idsToKeep, { duplicateId: null, ...assetUpdate });
```

The `AssetShare` check on `idsToKeep` is the tell. Someone asked whether the caller may act on the keeper,
applied the answer to the album add, and did not carry it twenty lines down to the two writes.

## Learning the group UUID

`mapAsset` masks `isFavorite` for non-owners at `asset-response.dto.ts:227` and then emits `duplicateId`
unmasked at line 240. So a plain viewer on a shared album reads it straight out of `POST /search/metadata`
with an `albumIds` filter, alongside `ownerId`. A partner can enumerate the sharer's whole library the same
way. No out-of-band knowledge is involved.

## Proof

Lab at v3.1.0, two ordinary accounts, victim shares one album with mallory as viewer.

Mallory reads the victim's `duplicateId` from the album search, stamps it on her own asset, and resolves:

```
PUT  /assets   ids=[mallory asset Z]  duplicateId=1111...      -> 204
POST /duplicates/resolve  keep=[victim asset X]  trash=[Z]     -> 200 success:true
```

Victim asset X before and after, fetched as the victim:

```
CHANGED exif.description: 'CANARY-VICTIM-DESC-7f3a' -> 'CANARY-VICTIM-DESC-7f3a\nPWNED-BY-MALLORY-9c2e'
CHANGED isFavorite: False -> True
CHANGED rating: 1 -> 5
CHANGED latitude/longitude: null -> 41.8902 / 12.4922, city Rome, country Italy
same    ownerId: b49f54bd-...  the asset is still the victim's
```

Only ids mallory legitimately holds are used, her own and the one visible in the shared album.

Negative controls:

- Direct write, `PUT /assets` on the victim asset: `400 Not found or no asset.update access`. The ordinary
  path is properly closed.
- Resolving a group she never joined: `400 Not found or no duplicate.delete access`. The membership gate
  does work, it is just the wrong question.
- An unrelated account handed the UUID out of band gets the same write, so the album share is the discovery
  channel and not an authorization prerequisite.

## Limits, stated up front

The full metadata merge only fires when `idsToKeep.length === 1`, per commit `cc8d3b410`, so the group has
to resolve to exactly one visible victim asset plus the planted one. The caller must also name every member
`get` returns or the call fails validation before writing anything. That is not much of a barrier in
practice: `get` excludes trashed, stacked and archived assets, so a victim who trashes one of a pair leaves
a single visible member, and `cleanupSingletonGroups` only runs when the owner opens the duplicates page.
Probing is free because a wrong guess writes nothing.

Multi-keeper groups still let the attacker null `duplicateId` on the victim's assets, quietly emptying their
duplicate review queue.

This is integrity only. Nothing is read that the attacker could not already read, ownership does not
transfer, and the attacker cannot trash the victim's assets because the `AssetDelete` check holds.

## Suggested fix

Give `get` a `userId` and require the caller to own every asset in the group, or run
`checkAccess(Permission.AssetUpdate)` over `idsToKeep` and drop the ids that fail before `updateAllExif`,
`updateAll` and `replaceAssetTags`.

## Severity

CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N, 6.0 Medium.

CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key, with CWE-862 Missing Authorization alongside.
